parameters.query:
INSERT INTO messages (whatsapp_message_id, phone_number, message_text)
VALUES ($1, $2, $3)
ON CONFLICT (whatsapp_message_id) DO NOTHING
RETURNING message_id;

nodes.name: Is New Message?
nodes.notes: TRUE = row returned = new message. FALSE = duplicate (ON CONFLICT hit nothing) -> stop.

parameters.query:
WITH patient AS (
  INSERT INTO patients (patient_name, whatsapp_number)
  VALUES ($1, $2)
  ON CONFLICT (whatsapp_number)
  DO UPDATE SET patient_name = COALESCE(patients.patient_name, EXCLUDED.patient_name)
  RETURNING patient_id, patient_name, whatsapp_number
)
UPDATE messages AS m
SET patient_id = p.patient_id
FROM patient AS p
WHERE m.message_id = $3
RETURNING p.patient_id, p.patient_name, p.whatsapp_number;

nodes.name: Is Text Message?
nodes.notes: TRUE = text message, proceed to Gemini NLU. FALSE = image/audio/document/etc -> ask patient to resend as text.

assignments.name: reply_text

nodes.name: Gemini Chat Model
nodes.notes: Select whichever free-tier Gemini model is actually listed in YOUR n8n Gemini credential/model dropdown. Do not assume a model name - pick from the live list.

options.systemMessage:
=You are a hospital appointment assistant for a WhatsApp booking demo.
Asia/Kolkata is the only timezone. The current date and time in Asia/Kolkata is {{ $now.setZone('Asia/Kolkata').toFormat('cccc, yyyy-LL-dd HH:mm') }}. Resolve all relative dates and times (today/tomorrow/Monday/tomorrow evening/etc.) against this current date/time.

You do not have access to any tools or the database. You ONLY understand the patient's natural-language request and extract structured intent/entities from it. You never decide doctor identity, availability, or booking success - deterministic backend logic handles all of that after you.

Default appointment duration is 30 minutes when only a start time is given.

Required information for BOOK or AVAILABILITY_CHECK: (doctor name OR specialization) AND a date AND a time. Do NOT ask for the patient's name - their WhatsApp number already identifies them. If any required piece is missing, set intent=MISSING_INFO and ask ONLY for the missing piece(s) in clarification_question.

If the patient is only asking about a specialization in general (e.g. "I need a cardiologist") with no specific date/time requested, set intent=SPECIALIZATION_SEARCH (date/time not required for this intent).

If the patient asks to cancel or reschedule an appointment, set intent=UNSUPPORTED and say in reply_text that this demo does not support that yet.

Always end your turn with ONLY a single raw JSON object (no prose, no markdown fences, no comments) with exactly this shape:
{
  "intent": "BOOK" | "AVAILABILITY_CHECK" | "SPECIALIZATION_SEARCH" | "MISSING_INFO" | "UNSUPPORTED",
  "doctor_name": string|null,
  "specialization": string|null,
  "requested_date": string|null,
  "requested_start_time": string|null,
  "requested_end_time": string|null,
  "clarification_question": string|null,
  "reply_text": string|null
}
requested_start_time and requested_end_time must be ISO8601 timestamps with the +05:30 offset when present. requested_end_time defaults to requested_start_time + 30 minutes if the patient did not state an end time.

nodes.name: Intent Router
nodes.notes: Outputs in order: 0=BOOK, 1=AVAILABILITY_CHECK, 2=SPECIALIZATION_SEARCH, 3=MISSING_INFO, 4=UNSUPPORTED, 5=fallback (unrecognized intent, should not normally happen).

parameters.query:
SELECT
  COUNT(*)::int AS match_count,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(*) = 1 THEN MAX(doctor_id) ELSE NULL END AS doctor_id,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(*) = 1 THEN MAX(doctor_name) ELSE NULL END AS doctor_name,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(*) = 1 THEN MAX(specialization) ELSE NULL END AS specialization,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(*) = 1 THEN MAX(google_calendar_id) ELSE NULL END AS google_calendar_id
FROM doctors
WHERE ($1::text IS NULL OR doctor_name ILIKE '%' || $1 || '%')
  AND ($2::text IS NULL OR specialization ILIKE '%' || $2 || '%');

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [$('Parse Agent Output').item.json.doctor_name || null, $('Parse Agent Output').item.json.specialization || null] }}

nodes.name: Count Doctor Matches
nodes.notes: PostgreSQL nodes return one item per row - never trust $json.length on the query's own output item. This node collapses 0/1/many rows into a single reliable item.

nodes.name: Doctor Match Count
nodes.notes: TRUE = exactly one match, proceed. FALSE = zero or multiple matches -> clarification message.

nodes.name: Set - Booking Context
nodes.notes: Explicitly constructs the booking context after the unique-doctor branch: __doctor_id and __google_calendar_id, sourced from the single doctor row resolved by Count Doctor Matches. includeOtherFields keeps matchCount/doctor_name/specialization alongside them. This is the single canonical source referenced by every downstream booking node that needs doctor identity.

assignments.name: reply_text
assignments.value: ={{ $json.matchCount === 0 ? "I couldn't find a matching doctor. Could you confirm the doctor's name or specialization?" : "I found more than one matching doctor. Could you confirm which one you mean?" }}

conditions.leftValue: ={{ (() => { const s = $('Parse Agent Output').item.json.requested_start_time; const e = $('Parse Agent Output').item.json.requested_end_time; if (!s || !e) return false; const sd = new Date(s); const ed = new Date(e); const now = new Date(); return Number.isFinite(sd.getTime()) && Number.isFinite(ed.getTime()) && ed.getTime() > sd.getTime() && sd.getTime() > now.getTime(); })() }}

nodes.name: Validate Date/Time Present
nodes.notes: Defensive backend guard: requires valid parseable timestamps, end > start, and start time strictly in the future. Prevents NULL/malformed/past appointments from reaching availability or booking.

assignments.name: reply_text
assignments.value: That date/time is missing, invalid, or already in the past. Please send a future appointment date and time (for example, tomorrow at 6 PM).

parameters.query:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS conflict_count
FROM appointments
WHERE doctor_id = $1
  AND status = 'SCHEDULED'
  AND start_time < $3
  AND end_time > $2;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [$('Set - Booking Context').item.json.__doctor_id, $('Parse Agent Output').item.json.requested_start_time, $('Parse Agent Output').item.json.requested_end_time] }}

assignments.name: reply_text
assignments.value: Sorry, something went wrong while scheduling that appointment. Please try again in a moment.

parameters.query:
WITH inserted AS (
  INSERT INTO appointments (
    patient_id, doctor_id, start_time, end_time, status, google_calendar_event_id
  )
  SELECT $1, $2, $3, $4, 'SCHEDULED', $5
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM appointments
    WHERE doctor_id = $2
      AND status = 'SCHEDULED'
      AND start_time < $4
      AND end_time > $3
  )
  ON CONFLICT (doctor_id, start_time) DO NOTHING
  RETURNING appointment_id, appointment_date
)
SELECT
  EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM inserted) AS booking_created,
  (SELECT appointment_id FROM inserted) AS appointment_id,
  (SELECT appointment_date FROM inserted) AS appointment_date;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [$('Find or Create Patient').item.json.patient_id, $('Set - Booking Context').item.json.__doctor_id, $('Parse Agent Output').item.json.requested_start_time, $('Parse Agent Output').item.json.requested_end_time, null] }}

nodes.name: Insert Appointment
nodes.notes: Database-first booking: this INSERT is the source of truth and runs before any Google Calendar event is created, so google_calendar_event_id is always NULL here and is saved back afterwards by 'Update Appointment Calendar Event ID'. Normal-path overlap protection is enforced again at INSERT time, so a slot that becomes occupied after the initial availability check is rejected. Since no Calendar event exists yet at this point, a lost race requires no Calendar cleanup.

nodes.name: Appointment Inserted?
nodes.notes: TRUE = PostgreSQL created the appointment. FALSE = the slot was lost to a concurrent/overlapping booking; clean up the already-created Calendar event and report failure.

assignments.name: reply_text
assignments.value: =Your appointment with Dr. {{$('Count Doctor Matches').item.json.doctor_name}} is confirmed for {{$('Parse Agent Output').item.json.requested_start_time}} (Asia/Kolkata).

nodes.name: Cancel Appointment (Calendar Sync Failed)
nodes.notes: Database-first booking means the appointment row already exists by the time Calendar sync can fail. Best-effort cancellation of that row so it is never left SCHEDULED without a synced Calendar event. If this also fails, we still do not claim the booking succeeded.

assignments.name: reply_text
assignments.value: Sorry, that slot was just booked by someone else. Could you suggest another time?

parameters.query:
UPDATE appointments
SET google_calendar_event_id = $1
WHERE appointment_id = $2
RETURNING appointment_id, google_calendar_event_id;

nodes.name: Update Appointment Calendar Event ID
nodes.notes: Runs only after Google Calendar - Create Event succeeds. Saves the returned Calendar event id back onto the appointment row created earlier by Insert Appointment, using its appointment_id.

nodes.name: Merge Reply Branches
nodes.notes: This is intentionally a pass-through convergence node. Each execution follows exactly one response branch; it does not wait for all branches like a two-input Merge node would.

nodes.name: Send WhatsApp Reply
nodes.notes: Only successful sends continue to Mark Message Processed. The frozen four-table demo intentionally does not implement an outbound outbox/idempotency table; therefore distributed send-vs-database crash recovery remains a known architectural limitation.

nodes.name: Was Message Inserted?
nodes.notes: Gate before Mark Message Processed. Non-text messages were never inserted into messages (no message_id), so they must not reach the UPDATE ... WHERE message_id = $1 step. TRUE = text message that was inserted earlier in the flow -> mark processed. FALSE = non-text message -> end, nothing to mark.
